title: Prove shortest S3 single-target word rigidity
body:
In the formal binary S3 rank-one-idempotent alphabet, the known three-call implementation of one longest-transposition target is rigid: for every register count, a three-call word must have labels `sts` or `tst`, and all three projectors must equal the target projector. This answers the shortest-word equality part of PR #4647's first open question; its shorter-word lower bound remains prior work.

The scoped package proves the result by six independent group-ring coefficients and supplies an independent faithful 18×18 binary-matrix census of all 175,616 three-register words. Each of the 28 rank-one targets has exactly two hits. It includes controls for dirty-scratch leakage, changed labels/projectors, rank-two outer factors, and representation/order mistakes.

Validation:
- Python 3.12 registered package replay and both direct scripts in normal and `-O` modes pass.
- Separate Codex review checked the proof and code, plus independent 8,192 arbitrary-matrix and 1,728 rank-one two-register cases.
- Committed-byte/source-history preflight and Git-free exported direct replay pass.

This is a scoped formal-algebra result. It does not supply native operation prices, a complete multiplier or a new κ; longer-word searches and Lean/Docker suites were not run. Only the new package directory changes.

Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4350#discussioncomment-19130285

Predecessor: #4647 at `734bb589d082ccd7c61b987d36a84b85c318e117`; local provenance and retained contributor credit are recorded in the package. Prepared for JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including a separate AI reviewer; no human or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

The refreshed matches and changed records did not identify another single-target three-call equality classification; this is bounded search coverage, not a novelty guarantee. Closed PR diffs and arbitrary nested code remain outside the search.
